Armstrong 500 Mount Panorama, Bathurst 6th October, 1963 Number of Laps: 130 Total Race Time: 7:46:99.10 Fastest lap: N
A Classes: Class A - Up to £900; Class B - £901 to £1000; Class C - £1001 to £1200; Class D - £1201 to £2000 In 1963 the race was moved to the Mount, at a time when both manufacturers

sponsors were beginning to understand the potential commercial gains to be made, such was the amount of support the race had so quickly garnered from the public. It was only natural for the manufacturers to want to have success on the Mountain, knowing only too well that a victory at this event would ensure sales the next day. Thus began the manufacture of "Bathurst Specials", cars designed specifically for the big race. The first came in 1963 with the Holden EH S4, which featured a 179ci engine
3.36:1 diff. Although 6 would be entered that year, it was the all conquering GT Cortina 1500 of Bob Jane
Harry Firth that would take the honours. Please Note: You can sort this listing by simply clicking on the column heading PLACE DRIVER
